# NetSimR

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![CRAN
status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/NetSimR)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=NetSimR)
[![CRAN
downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/NetSimR)](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/NetSimR)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR)

NetSimR is an R package of actuarial functions for non-life insurance
and reinsurance pricing, reserving and capital modelling, with six Shiny
tools for simulating claims, fitting distributions and GLMs, reserving,
pricing excess of loss reinsurance and the capital of a portfolio. Its
website, with every help page and the vignettes, is
<https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/>, where the tools can also
be [tried in the
browser](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/try-online.html),
with nothing to install.

**Your data stays on your computer.** The tools run on your own machine:
in R or, on the website, in an R that runs inside your browser. A file
you open in a tool is read there and is not sent anywhere. [How this
works](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/try-online.html#your-data-stays-on-your-computer).

[![Try the Shiny apps in your browser, nothing to
install](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%96%B6%20Try%20the%20Shiny%20apps-in%20your%20browser%2C%20nothing%20to%20install-2563eb?style=for-the-badge)](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/try-online.html)

## Installation

``` r

# the released version from CRAN
install.packages("NetSimR")

# the development version from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR")
```

## What it does

- **Capped means, exposure curves and increased limit factors (ILFs)**
  for LogNormal, Gamma, Pareto, sliced LogNormal-Pareto and sliced
  Gamma-Pareto claim sizes.
- **Sliced distributions**: mean, density, cdf and quantile function of
  the sliced LogNormal-Pareto and Gamma-Pareto distributions.
- **Pure IBNR exposure** from a LogNormal or Gamma reporting delay.
- **Claims simulation** with a frequency-severity model, Pareto tail
  slices, a severity cap, each-and-every-loss layers with reinstatements
  and their premiums, aggregate layers, and each period’s largest claim
  (OEP), run in parallel when that is faster; portfolios of several
  lines joined by a Gaussian or t copula, with VaR, TVaR,
  diversification and capital allocation.
- **Claims reserving**: the chain ladder with Mack’s standard errors and
  tail factors, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, Benktander and Cape Cod, a
  bootstrap of the reserves’ distribution, the one-year view
  (Merz-Wuthrich), the Munich chain ladder of paid and incurred claims,
  Clark’s growth curves, a chain ladder for claims inflation, and actual
  against expected development.
- **IFRS 17 and Solvency II**: reserves discounted with a yield curve,
  the risk adjustment by percentile or cost of capital, and the standard
  formula’s non-life premium and reserve risk.
- **Pricing models and rate reviews**: a Tweedie family for GLMs of the
  loss cost, on-level premiums by the parallelogram method, the
  indicated rate change, and Buhlmann-Straub credibility.
- **Reinsurance programmes** compared by their cost and the capital they
  save.
- **Excess of loss pricing**: the burning cost with indexation,
  development and aggregate terms, a Pareto model of the large losses,
  exposure rating with the Swiss Re and Lloyd’s (MBBEFD) curves or a
  claim size distribution, credibility blending and the technical
  premium with reinstatements.
- **Six Shiny tools**: NetSimulator, a claims simulator with reports and
  run comparison; NetDisFit, a distribution fitting tool for claim
  counts and sizes, including claims reported only above a threshold or
  capped at policy limits, with Q-Q and P-P plots, Anderson-Darling
  tests and the conditional tail expectations of each fit, whose fits it
  saves as simulator settings; NetGLM, a GLM fitting tool with a Tweedie
  family, splines and bands, variable selection (stepwise, lasso,
  elastic net, ridge), validation on held-out rows (Gini, lift and
  double lift), a rate table and scoring of new data; NetReserve, a
  reserving tool with a report; NetTreaty, a reinsurance pricing tool;
  and NetCapital, a portfolio capital tool with copulas and capital
  allocation.

## Examples

``` r

library(NetSimR)

# mean claim size capped at 600 for a Pareto with scale 200 and shape 1.2
# (the older CamelCase names, such as ParetoCappedMean(), still work)
pareto_capped_mean(600, 200, 1.2)

# increased limit factor from 700 to 1,000 for Gamma claim sizes
ilf_gamma(700, 1000, 1, 0.0005)

# Gamma body sliced at 3,000 with a Pareto tail of shape 1.4
psliced_gamma_pareto(5000, 1.2, 0.0004, 3000, 1.4)

# pure IBNR exposure (in days) of three periods, with a Gamma reporting delay
pure_ibnr_gamma(
  as.Date(c("2006-01-01", "2006-07-01", "2007-01-01")),
  as.Date(c("2006-12-31", "2007-06-30", "2007-12-31")),
  as.Date("2007-10-30"),
  shape = 7, rate = 0.15
)

# 10,000 years of Poisson claim counts with LogNormal claim sizes, a Pareto tail
# above 100,000, and a layer of 50,000 excess of 20,000 on each claim with two
# reinstatements at 100% of an upfront premium of 10,000
ceded <- simulate_claims(
  10000, "Poisson", 3, "LogNormal", c(meanlog = 8, sdlog = 1.5), seed = 1,
  pareto_thresholds = 100000, pareto_alphas = 1.5,
  eel_layer = "limited", eel_deductible = 20000, eel_limit = 50000,
  eel_reinstatements = 2, eel_premium = 10000
)
mean(ceded$total_claims)
mean(ceded$reinstatement_premium)

# chain ladder reserves of the RAA triangle with Mack's standard errors and a
# fitted tail, then the 99.5th percentile of the bootstrapped total reserve
chain_ladder(raa_triangle, tail = "exponential")
bootstrap_chain_ladder(raa_triangle, n = 10000, seed = 1)$total[["p99.5"]]

# the one-year view of the same reserves, and paid and incurred claims projected together
merz_wuthrich(raa_triangle)$total
munich_chain_ladder(quarg_mack_paid, quarg_mack_incurred)$total

# a layer of 4m excess of 1m priced on its experience and on a property risk
# profile with the Swiss Re Y3 exposure curve
burning_cost(xl_large_losses, xl_premium[, c("year", "premium")], 1e6, 4e6,
             inflation = 0.04, rating_premium = 60e6)
property_exposure_rating(xl_property_profile, 1e6, 4e6, curve = "Y3", loss_ratio = 0.55)
```

## Shiny tools

``` r

run_shiny_simulator()                  # NetSimulator: claims simulation
run_shiny_distribution_fitting_tool()  # NetDisFit: frequency and severity fits
run_shiny_glm_fitting_tool()           # NetGLM: generalised linear models
run_shiny_reserving_tool()             # NetReserve: claims reserving
run_shiny_reinsurance_pricing_tool()   # NetTreaty: reinsurance pricing
run_shiny_portfolio_tool()             # NetCapital: portfolio capital
```

Problems and ideas are welcome as [GitHub
issues](https://github.com/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR/issues/new/choose);
each tool’s About card links to them.

## Vignettes

Eight vignettes set out the theory behind the functions and work through
examples:

- *From pricing to capital and reserves: a motor portfolio*, which
  follows one portfolio through the package
- *Rate reviews: on-level premiums, the indicated rate change and
  credibility*
- *Capped means, exposure curves and increased limit factors*
- *Sliced LogNormal-Pareto and Gamma-Pareto distributions*
- *Pure IBNR exposure from a reporting delay distribution*
- *Simulating claims with simulate_claims()*
- *Claims reserving with the chain ladder and its relatives*
- *Pricing an excess of loss layer*

They are on the package’s [CRAN
page](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=NetSimR), and
`browseVignettes("NetSimR")` opens the copies installed with the package
(a development version installed from GitHub has them only when
installed with `build_vignettes = TRUE`).

## References

The methods are described in articles by Yiannis Parizas in *The
Actuary*: [Free for All](https://www.theactuary.com/2023/03/02/free-all)
(2023), [Escaping the
triangle](https://www.theactuary.com/features/2019/06/2019/06/05/escaping-triangle)
(2019) and [Taken to
excess](https://www.theactuary.com/features/2019/03/2019/03/06/taken-excess)
(2019).

## How to cite

If NetSimR helps your work, please cite it; `citation("NetSimR")` gives
the reference for the version installed, and a BibTeX entry:

> Parizas, Y. (2026). NetSimR: Non-Life Actuarial Pricing, Reserving,
> Reinsurance and Capital. R package version 0.4.0.
> <https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.NetSimR>

A star on [GitHub](https://github.com/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR) or a
mention to a colleague also helps others find it.

# Package index

## Shiny tools

Applications that run the package’s models without writing code.

- [`run_shiny_simulator()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/run_shiny_simulator.md)
  : Run the claims simulator application
- [`run_shiny_distribution_fitting_tool()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/run_shiny_distribution_fitting_tool.md)
  : Run the distribution fitting application
- [`run_shiny_glm_fitting_tool()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/run_shiny_glm_fitting_tool.md)
  : Run the generalised linear model fitting application
- [`run_shiny_reserving_tool()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/run_shiny_reserving_tool.md)
  : Run the claims reserving application
- [`run_shiny_reinsurance_pricing_tool()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/run_shiny_reinsurance_pricing_tool.md)
  : Run the reinsurance pricing application
- [`run_shiny_portfolio_tool()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/run_shiny_portfolio_tool.md)
  : Run the portfolio capital application

## Claims simulation and reinsurance

Frequency-severity simulation with Pareto tails, caps and layers, and
portfolios of lines joined by a copula.

- [`simulate_claims()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/simulate_claims.md)
  : Simulate claims with a frequency-severity model
- [`simulate_function()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/simulate_function.md)
  : Simulate insurance claims with reinsurance structures
- [`simulate_portfolio()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/simulate_portfolio.md)
  : Simulate a portfolio of dependent lines
- [`apply_deductible_limit()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/apply_deductible_limit.md)
  : Apply a deductible and limit to claims
- [`reinstatement_premium()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/reinstatement_premium.md)
  : Reinstatement premiums of an excess of loss layer
- [`compare_reinsurance()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/compare_reinsurance.md)
  : Compare reinsurance programmes

## Claims reserving

Chain ladder with Mack’s standard errors, methods with premiums, the
bootstrap, the one-year view, the Munich chain ladder, Clark’s growth
curves, inflation and actual vs expected.

- [`chain_ladder()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/chain_ladder.md)
  : Chain ladder reserves with Mack's standard errors
- [`bornhuetter_ferguson()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/bornhuetter_ferguson.md)
  : Bornhuetter-Ferguson and Benktander reserves
- [`cape_cod()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/cape_cod.md)
  : Cape Cod reserves
- [`bootstrap_chain_ladder()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/bootstrap_chain_ladder.md)
  : Bootstrap of the chain ladder reserves
- [`merz_wuthrich()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/merz_wuthrich.md)
  : The one-year view of the reserves: Merz and Wuthrich's claims
  development result
- [`munich_chain_ladder()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/munich_chain_ladder.md)
  : Munich chain ladder of paid and incurred claims
- [`actual_vs_expected()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/actual_vs_expected.md)
  : Actual against expected development
- [`clark_growth()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/clark_growth.md)
  : Clark's growth curve reserves
- [`inflation_adjusted_chain_ladder()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/inflation_adjusted_chain_ladder.md)
  : Chain ladder for claims inflation
- [`as_triangle()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/as_triangle.md)
  : Build a claims triangle from a table

## IFRS 17 and Solvency II

Discounted reserves, the risk adjustment, and the standard formula’s
non-life premium and reserve risk.

- [`discount_reserves()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/discount_reserves.md)
  : Discounted reserves from the chain ladder's payment pattern
- [`risk_adjustment()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/risk_adjustment.md)
  : Risk adjustment for non-financial risk
- [`sii_premium_reserve_risk()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/sii_premium_reserve_risk.md)
  : Solvency II standard formula: non-life premium and reserve risk
- [`sii_nonlife_segments`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/sii_nonlife_segments.md)
  [`sii_nonlife_correlation`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/sii_nonlife_segments.md)
  : The Solvency II standard formula's non-life segments

## Excess of loss pricing

Burning cost, Pareto rating, exposure rating with MBBEFD curves or a
claim size distribution, and the technical premium.

- [`burning_cost()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/burning_cost.md)
  : Burning cost of an excess of loss layer
- [`pareto_rating()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/pareto_rating.md)
  : Pareto rating of an excess of loss layer
- [`property_exposure_rating()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/property_exposure_rating.md)
  [`casualty_exposure_rating()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/property_exposure_rating.md)
  : Exposure rating of property and casualty excess of loss layers
- [`mbbefd_curve()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/mbbefd_curve.md)
  [`swiss_re_parameters()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/mbbefd_curve.md)
  [`swiss_re_curve()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/mbbefd_curve.md)
  : MBBEFD exposure curves
- [`technical_premium()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/technical_premium.md)
  : Technical premium of an excess of loss layer
- [`credibility_weight()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/credibility_weight.md)
  : Credibility of the loss experience

## Pricing models and rate reviews

A Tweedie family for generalised linear models of the loss cost,
on-level premiums, the indicated rate change and Buhlmann-Straub
credibility.

- [`tweedie_family()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/tweedie_family.md)
  : Tweedie family for generalised linear models
- [`on_level_premium()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/on_level_premium.md)
  : Premiums at today's rates: the parallelogram method
- [`indicated_rate_change()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/indicated_rate_change.md)
  : The indicated rate change: the loss ratio method
- [`buhlmann_straub()`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/buhlmann_straub.md)
  : Buhlmann-Straub credibility

## Data sets

- [`raa_triangle`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/raa_triangle.md)
  : RAA triangle of incurred claims
- [`taylor_ashe_triangle`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/taylor_ashe_triangle.md)
  : Taylor and Ashe triangle of paid claims
- [`quarg_mack_paid`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/quarg_mack.md)
  [`quarg_mack_incurred`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/quarg_mack.md)
  : Paid and incurred triangles of the Munich chain ladder paper
- [`simulated_motor_claims`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/simulated_motor_claims.md)
  : Simulated motor claims with premiums
- [`xl_large_losses`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/xl_large_losses.md)
  : Simulated large losses of an excess of loss treaty
- [`xl_premium`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/xl_premium.md)
  : Subject premiums of an excess of loss treaty
- [`xl_property_profile`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/xl_property_profile.md)
  : Risk profile of a property portfolio
- [`xl_casualty_profile`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/xl_casualty_profile.md)
  : Risk profile of a casualty portfolio
- [`motor_policies`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/motor_policies.md)
  : Simulated motor policies
- [`liability_claims`](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/reference/liability_claims.md)
  : Simulated liability claims at their policy limits

# Articles

### Articles

- [From pricing to capital and reserves: a motor
  portfolio](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/EndToEnd.md):

  A motor portfolio through a non-life actuary’s work in R: GLM pricing,
  claims simulation, excess of loss reinsurance, capital, reserves, IFRS
  17 and Solvency II.

- [Rate reviews: on-level premiums, the indicated rate change and
  credibility](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/PricingMonitoring.md):

  A rate review with the loss ratio method in R: on-level premiums by
  the parallelogram method, trended losses, the indicated rate change
  and credibility.

- [Simulating claims with
  simulate_claims()](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/SimulateClaims.md):

  Simulating insurance claims in R: frequency and severity
  distributions, Pareto tails, caps, and excess of loss layers with
  limited reinstatements.

- [Claims reserving with the chain ladder and its
  relatives](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/Reserving.md):

  Claims reserving in R: the chain ladder with Mack’s standard errors,
  Bornhuetter-Ferguson, Cape Cod, the bootstrap, the one-year view and
  the Munich chain ladder.

- [Pricing an excess of loss
  layer](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/ReinsurancePricing.md):

  Pricing an excess of loss layer in R: burning cost, Pareto rating,
  exposure rating with a risk profile, credibility and the technical
  premium.

- [Capped means, exposure curves and increased limit
  factors](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/CappedMean.md):

  Capped means, exposure curves and increased limit factors for
  LogNormal, Gamma, Pareto and sliced severities, with the theory and
  worked examples in R.

- [Sliced LogNormal-Pareto and Gamma-Pareto
  distributions](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/SlicedDistributions.md):

  Sliced LogNormal-Pareto and Gamma-Pareto distributions for claim
  severities with a heavy tail: densities, distribution functions,
  quantiles and means in R.

- [Pure IBNR exposure from a reporting delay
  distribution](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/PureIBNR.md):

  Pure IBNR claim counts and unearned exposure from a LogNormal or Gamma
  reporting delay distribution, with the theory and worked examples in
  R.

### Shiny tools

- [Try the Shiny tools in your
  browser](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/try-online.md):

  The package’s six Shiny tools, running in your browser with webR: no R
  to install, and your data never leaves your computer.

- [A worked example: the six tools and their
  reports](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/worked-example.md):

  The six Shiny tools of NetSimR run on the package’s example data, from
  pricing to reserves, with the report each one writes.

### Custom tools

- [Custom tools for insurers and
  reinsurers](https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/articles/custom-tools.md):

  Pricing, reserving, reinsurance and capital tools built around your
  data, methods and governance.
